Let Hank know the courts are done.

missions.title: A Word with Grandmother
missions.description: Theo wants to enter the junior championship. Someone has to tell Mrs. Wellington. Apparently that's you.

steps.prompt: Talk to Theo.
Head to the patio, where Mrs. Wellington holds court.
Bring up Theo's tennis with Mrs. Wellington.
What do you tell Mrs. Wellington?

choices.label: The truth: he's good, and he loves it
choices.result: Mrs. Wellington is quiet for a long moment. "His grandfather played like that," she says at last. "I shall... consider it."

choices.label: Suggest Coach Rafa assesses him
choices.result: An expert opinion suits her perfectly. She books Coach Rafa for a "proper assessment" this evening. Theo looks like he might faint.

choices.label: Stay out of family business
choices.result: You make polite noises about the weather. Mrs. Wellington signs Theo up for another lunch. Theo sees it all from behind the fountain.

Collect fresh towels from the pro shop.
Lay the towels out on Court 1.
Wish Theo luck.
Check in with Mrs. Wellington after the set.

missions.title: The Brandt Line Call
missions.description: Newlyweds Leo and Harper Brandt need a neutral party for a disputed line call on Court 2. It's 'for the marriage'.

steps.prompt: Head to Court 2.
Hear Leo's side.
Hear Harper's side.
Make the call.

choices.label: It clipped the line. In.
choices.result: Harper cheers. Leo stares at the line for a long time, then laughs. "Okay, counsel. Your point."

choices.label: Out, by a hair.
choices.result: Leo pumps his fist like he won Wimbledon. Harper narrows her eyes and adds a tally mark to her spreadsheet.

choices.label: Too close to call. Play a let.
choices.result: They replay the point. Harper lobs him again, clearly in this time. Leo applauds. Both look delighted.

steps.prompt: Hear Harper's plan.
Pick up the sparkling water Jess is hiding at the pro shop.
Set up the picnic by the garden fountain.
Casually steer Leo toward the garden.
Tell Harper he's on his way.

steps.prompt: Head to the garden.
Talk to Babs about the flower beds.
Get Diane's side.

choices.label: Split the bed down the middle
choices.result: Roses on the north side, hydrangeas on the south. Both women inspect the border line with a ruler. Peace, of a kind.

choices.label: Let Maria decide as co-chair
choices.result: Maria, delighted to be asked, picks hydrangeas "for the koi". Babs beams. Diane writes something in her notebook.

choices.label: Roses were there first
choices.result: Diane nods as if this were obvious. Babs says "Mm-hmm" in a way that promises the story will be all over the patio by lunch.

missions.title: Gloria's Wooden Racket
missions.description: Gloria Castellano's 1968 wooden racket snapped a string. It's on the Court 5 bench and it needs Jess, carefully.

steps.prompt: Talk to Gloria.
Collect Gloria's wooden racket from Court 5. Gently.
Take the racket to Jess at the pro shop.
Hand the racket over to Jess.

missions.title: Section 7.3
missions.description: Frank DeLuca has cited Kevin Park under bylaw 7.3, 'appropriate tennis attire'. Again. Kevin is hiding by the pro shop.

steps.prompt: Hear Frank's report.
Find Kevin and hear his side.
How do you handle the dress code dispute?

choices.label: Loan Kevin whites from the pro shop
choices.result: Kevin emerges in head-to-toe whites, looking like a 1978 tournament poster. Frank salutes. Kevin isn't sure how to feel.

choices.label: Point out 7.3 was amended in 2009
choices.result: Frank checks his binder. Then checks it again. "Amended," he says, like a man betrayed. Kevin does a very small victory dance.

choices.label: Compromise: tuck the shirt in
choices.result: Kevin tucks. Frank inspects. "Marginal," he says, and walks off. From Frank, that's practically a hug.

steps.prompt: Meet Lily. And Barbara.
Pick up Barbara (the ball hopper) at Court 4.
Give Barbara a home in the equipment shed.
Let Maria know where her daughter has been.

steps.prompt: Talk to Dr. Rao before he runs.

Leave the racket at the pro shop for safekeeping.
Break the news to Nate.

choices.label: Find Theo for him

choices.result: You feed forty forehands. Nate thanks you politely and logs it as "sub-optimal, appreciated".

choices.label: Suggest he call it a day
choices.result: Nate looks at you like you suggested he skip a banana. He goes for a run instead.

steps.prompt: Head to the members' lounge in the clubhouse.
Hear Gloria out about the fireside armchairs.
How do you settle the seating?

choices.label: First come, first served

theo_practice_1.speaker: Theo Wellington
theo_practice_1.text: Hey. Okay, so. I'm supposed to be at etiquette lunch right now.

theo_practice_1.speaker: Theo Wellington
theo_practice_1.text: But the junior championship is in three weeks and my second serve is a disaster. I need a ball hopper on Court 1.

theo_practice_1.speaker: Theo Wellington
theo_practice_1.text: Quietly. If Grandma sees a hopper with my name near it, I'm doing napkin folding until I'm thirty.

theo_practice_2.speaker: Theo Wellington
theo_practice_2.text: You got it? No way. Thanks. Seriously.

theo_practice_2.speaker: Theo Wellington
theo_practice_2.text: Nate says you need five hundred second serves a week. I'm at forty. ...Don't tell anyone I said thanks.

theo_grandma_1.speaker: Theo Wellington
theo_grandma_1.text: So... I signed up for the junior championship. With my allowance. Grandma doesn't know.

theo_grandma_1.speaker: Theo Wellington
theo_grandma_1.text: She's on the patio. She likes you. Well, she hasn't complained about you in, like, two days.

theo_grandma_1.speaker: Theo Wellington
theo_grandma_1.text: Could you... bring it up? Casually? I'll be behind the fountain. Not hiding. Just... near the fountain.

theo_grandma_2.speaker: Mrs. Wellington
theo_grandma_2.text: The attendant. You have the expression of someone about to say something I won't like.

theo_grandma_2.speaker: Mrs. Wellington
theo_grandma_2.text: Theodore? Tennis? He has etiquette lunch. He has sailing. He has Latin.

theo_grandma_2.speaker: Mrs. Wellington
theo_grandma_2.text: ...His grandfather used to sneak off to play, too. Well? Out with it.

theo_exhibition_1.speaker: Coach Rafa Ibarra
theo_exhibition_1.text: Ah, my friend. You have heard? Theo plays an exhibition set on Court 1. His grandmother will watch.

theo_exhibition_1.speaker: Coach Rafa Ibarra
theo_exhibition_1.text: Whatever you told her, it worked. She asked me what 'topspin' is. I told her it is a way of life.

theo_exhibition_1.speaker: Coach Rafa Ibarra
theo_exhibition_1.text: Bring fresh towels from the shop. If Mrs. Wellington sits on a damp bench, Theo's career is over before it begins.

theo_exhibition_2.speaker: Theo Wellington
theo_exhibition_2.text: She's actually here. In the front row. With a cushion she brought from home.

theo_exhibition_2.speaker: Theo Wellington
theo_exhibition_2.text: Okay. Okay. Five hundred second serves. The ball has no memory. I can do this.

theo_exhibition_3.speaker: Mrs. Wellington
theo_exhibition_3.text: Six games to two. He served eleven aces. I counted. Rafa told me what an ace is.

theo_exhibition_3.speaker: Mrs. Wellington
theo_exhibition_3.text: I have informed the etiquette instructor that Theodore will be unavailable on tournament weekends.

theo_exhibition_3.speaker: Mrs. Wellington
theo_exhibition_3.text: You were... helpful today, attendant. Do not let it go to your head.

brandt_call_1.speaker: Leo Brandt
brandt_call_1.text: Oh good, a neutral party. Harper lobbed me on set point. It landed behind the baseline. OUT.

brandt_call_1.speaker: Leo Brandt
brandt_call_1.text: I had a perfect sightline. Pilots have excellent depth perception. It's literally tested.

brandt_call_2.speaker: Harper Brandt
brandt_call_2.text: Okay but he was running BACKWARDS. His depth perception was aimed at the fence.

brandt_call_2.speaker: Harper Brandt
brandt_call_2.text: It clipped the line. There's a mark. I'd like the mark entered into evidence.

brandt_call_2.speaker: Harper Brandt
brandt_call_2.text: Whatever you decide, he's going to bring it up at Thanksgiving. So, you know. No pressure.

brandt_anniv_1.speaker: Harper Brandt
brandt_anniv_1.text: Psst! Okay, so today's our six-month anniversary, and Leo thinks I forgot. I did not forget.

brandt_anniv_1.speaker: Harper Brandt
brandt_anniv_1.text: I'm doing a surprise picnic by the fountain. Jess is hiding sparkling water behind the stringing machine for me.

brandt_anniv_1.speaker: Harper Brandt
brandt_anniv_1.text: Can you set it up in the garden, then steer Leo over? He'll be the one in lime, arguing with something.

brandt_anniv_2.speaker: Leo Brandt
brandt_anniv_2.text: Hey. Have you seen Harper? She's been weird all day. Weird-happy. Should I be worried?

brandt_anniv_2.speaker: Leo Brandt
brandt_anniv_2.text: The garden? Why would I... oh. OH. Is today... It's today. I'm going. I'm going right now.

brandt_anniv_3.speaker: Harper Brandt
brandt_anniv_3.text: He's coming? Did he remember? He didn't remember. It's okay, that's the whole point of surprises!

brandt_anniv_3.speaker: Harper Brandt
brandt_anniv_3.text: Thank you! You're getting the first slice of cake. Unless Leo eats it. He stress-eats when he's grateful.

flower_feud_1.speaker: Babs Hendricks
flower_feud_1.text: Oh, honey, thank goodness. You won't BELIEVE what Diane did to my hydrangeas.

flower_feud_1.speaker: Babs Hendricks
flower_feud_1.text: She pulled up two of them and planted roses. ROSES. Lily saw the whole thing. She's a very reliable witness. She's ten.

flower_feud_1.speaker: Babs Hendricks
flower_feud_1.text: Hydrangeas are the club flower. Well, they're MY flower. Same thing.

flower_feud_2.speaker: Diane Ross
flower_feud_2.text: That bed has had roses since 1987. I planted them. As president. Of the club. For six terms.

flower_feud_2.speaker: Diane Ross
flower_feud_2.text: Babs slipped her hydrangeas in while I was at the dentist. That's not gardening. That's a coup.

gloria_racket_1.speaker: Gloria Castellano
gloria_racket_1.text: Darling. My racket has broken a string. The racket is from 1968. So am I, spiritually.

gloria_racket_1.speaker: Gloria Castellano
gloria_racket_1.text: It's on the Court 5 bench. Carry it like a newborn. Jess is the only person I trust to restring it.

gloria_racket_1.speaker: Gloria Castellano
gloria_racket_1.text: And if Frank asks, I'm not forfeiting. I'm merely... pausing my dominance.

gloria_racket_2.speaker: Jess Nakamura
gloria_racket_2.text: Oh. The Maxply. Hi, old friend.

gloria_racket_2.speaker: Jess Nakamura
gloria_racket_2.text: Gut strings, 50 pounds, hand-knotted. Tell Gloria tomorrow morning. Tell her I said 'with respect'. She'll know.

dress_code_1.speaker: Frank DeLuca
dress_code_1.text: Attendant. Report. The Park boy is in violation of section 7.3, appropriate tennis attire.

dress_code_1.speaker: Frank DeLuca
dress_code_1.text: Cargo shorts, son. With eight pockets. I counted. Nobody needs eight pockets on a tennis court.

dress_code_1.speaker: Frank DeLuca
dress_code_1.text: I'm not unreasonable. I'm by the book. Take care of it.

dress_code_2.speaker: Kevin Park
dress_code_2.text: Is he gone? Oh no, he sent you. Okay. Okay.

dress_code_2.speaker: Kevin Park
dress_code_2.text: They're technical shorts! The pockets are for my phone, my backup phone, and my serve notebook.

dress_code_2.speaker: Kevin Park
dress_code_2.text: Priya says the dress code was changed years ago, but I can't find it anywhere. Nobody tells us anything...

lily_balls_1.speaker: Lily Santos
lily_balls_1.text: HI! This is Barbara! She's a ball bucket! She has FORTY-SEVEN balls in her!

lily_balls_1.speaker: Lily Santos
lily_balls_1.text: I found them in the hedges and under benches and one was in the fountain, but Gerald didn't want it.

lily_balls_1.speaker: Lily Santos
lily_balls_1.text: Barbara's at Court 4 and she's too heavy now. Can you take her to the shed? She needs a home. A good home.

lily_balls_2.speaker: Maria Santos
lily_balls_2.text: Forty-seven balls? From the hedges? That explains the scratches on her arms. And the leaves in her hair.

lily_balls_2.speaker: Maria Santos
lily_balls_2.text: Thank you for humoring her. She's going to tell everyone Barbara lives in the shed now. Hank will love that.

vik_paged_1.speaker: Dr. Vik Rao
vik_paged_1.text: I am so sorry, I have to go. Compound fracture. Mid-serve, again. The pager has impeccable timing.

vik_paged_1.speaker: Dr. Vik Rao
vik_paged_1.text: My racket's on Court 2. Could you get it to the pro shop? Jess keeps it safe from Chad.

vik_paged_1.speaker: Dr. Vik Rao
vik_paged_1.text: And tell Nate I'm sorry. He was warmed up. He hates wasting a warm-up. Medically, he's right.

vik_paged_2.speaker: Nate Okafor
vik_paged_2.text: Paged again? That's fifteen this season.

vik_paged_2.speaker: Nate Okafor
vik_paged_2.text: I'm fully warmed up. Heart rate's in the zone. It'd be a shame to waste it.

lesson_setup_1.speaker: Priya Sharma
lesson_setup_1.text: Oh, the hopper's out already? Thank you! Rafa says today is 'the day of the backhand'.

lesson_setup_1.speaker: Priya Sharma
lesson_setup_1.text: Last week was 'the day of the split step'. I split-stepped into the net. He said it was 'progress, in a way'.

opening_briefing.speaker: Hank Morris
opening_briefing.text: Morning! Clay took a beating yesterday, so keep an eye on Courts 3 to 5.

opening_briefing.speaker: Hank Morris
opening_briefing.text: Rush hours are mid-morning and late afternoon. The radio gets busy then, so pace yourself.

reservation_dispute_1.speaker: Mrs. Wellington
reservation_dispute_1.text: I have had this court reserved for WEEKS. And now this person just walks on?

reservation_dispute_1.speaker: Mrs. Wellington
reservation_dispute_1.text: Check the schedule. You'll see I'm right.

reservation_dispute_2.speaker: Kevin Park
reservation_dispute_2.text: Oh no, am I on the wrong court? The app said Court 3...

reservation_dispute_2.speaker: Kevin Park
reservation_dispute_2.text: I'm so sorry, I'm still figuring out how this place works.

patio_argument_1.speaker: Chad Blake
patio_argument_1.text: Bro, I was literally sitting here first. I went to grab a drink for TWO seconds.

patio_argument_1.speaker: Chad Blake
patio_argument_1.text: Tell her this is my table.

patio_argument_2.speaker: Diane Ross
patio_argument_2.text: This young man abandoned his table. I sat down. That's how it works.

patio_argument_2.speaker: Diane Ross
patio_argument_2.text: I've been a member here since before he was born.

wrong_court_1.speaker: Priya Sharma
wrong_court_1.text: Hey! So I signed up for Court 1 but... I think I'm on Court 3?

wrong_court_1.speaker: Priya Sharma
wrong_court_1.text: All these courts look the same to me! Is this the clay one? What's clay?

noise_complaint_1.speaker: Diane Ross
noise_complaint_1.text: Do you HEAR that racket? No pun intended.

noise_complaint_1.speaker: Diane Ross
noise_complaint_1.text: That person on Court 2 is grunting like a wild animal. Handle it.

noise_complaint_2.speaker: Tommy Chen
noise_complaint_2.text: Oh man, was I being loud? I get into the zone sometimes!

noise_complaint_2.speaker: Tommy Chen
noise_complaint_2.text: My bad, my bad. What do you think I should do?

groom_intro_1.speaker: Hank Morris
groom_intro_1.text: Good, you're here. All three clay courts have been getting hammered — slides, divots, the works.

groom_intro_1.speaker: Hank Morris
groom_intro_1.text: Head to the equipment shed and hook up the drag brush. Then start at the fence perimeter and work your way in.

groom_intro_1.speaker: Hank Morris
groom_intro_1.text: After the perimeter, sweep close to the nets on each court. Then fill in the middles. Don't forget to swap the coolers and check the trash bins between courts!

groom_complete_1.speaker: Hank Morris
groom_complete_1.text: Let me take a look... nice work out there. All three courts look great.

groom_complete_1.speaker: Hank Morris
groom_complete_1.text: Keep it up and you'll be running the grounds crew in no time.

morning_prep_1.speaker: Hank Morris
morning_prep_1.text: Big morning ahead — all three clay courts need grooming before the 9 AM group.

morning_prep_1.speaker: Hank Morris
morning_prep_1.text: Grab the brush, start at the fence line, and sweep your way in toward the nets. Remember to check the coolers and trash between courts.

morning_prep_1.speaker: Hank Morris
morning_prep_1.text: I'll be checking your work when you're done, so make it count!

morning_prep_done.speaker: Hank Morris
morning_prep_done.text: All three courts done? Let me see...

morning_prep_done.speaker: Hank Morris
morning_prep_done.text: Looking sharp! The members are going to love playing on that surface today. Good job.

bldg_lounge_fireplace_1.speaker: Gloria Castellano
bldg_lounge_fireplace_1.text: Thirty years I have sat in that chair by the fire. Thirty years!

bldg_lounge_fireplace_1.speaker: Gloria Castellano
bldg_lounge_fireplace_1.text: And today some teenager is doing his homework in it with a smoothie. On the leather.

bldg_lounge_fireplace_1.speaker: Gloria Castellano
bldg_lounge_fireplace_1.text: I'm not asking for a plaque, dear. Although a plaque would be lovely.
